subject: Interim transit authorization & 96h buffer request for EU-residency datasets
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@datagrove.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@datagrove.com
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2027 08:15:00 -0500
Subject: Interim transit authorization & 96h buffer for EU-residency datasets

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We are close to a procurement decision but Legal and Security have two outstanding asks before we can sign the DPA addendum:

1) Confirm whether Redwood can support a planned 96-hour temporary transit window for analytics re-ingestion and short-lived reprocessing that may route data outside the EU (we expect this to be telemetry/analytics only, not primary PII processing).
2) Provide the latest subprocessor roster and an ops playbook describing the transient-egress safeguards (telemetry retention, KMS handoff, per-request audit keys, and notification SLA).
3) Evidence — Legal wants an example of the audit artifact we would receive if this transient hop occurs (sample log packet and retention proof).

Can you share the DPA addendum draft and the subprocessor CSV? If Redwood cannot make 96h a committed window, please propose an operational alternative (e.g., 72h + escalation path). Our compliance deadline for execution is Dec 10th.

Appreciate a clear list of next steps and who will need to sign. If you can route the addendum to procurement (procurement@datagrove.com) via DocuSign, that would speed things.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Head of Security & Compliance
Datagrove

Attachments: none
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@datagrove.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2027 11:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Interim transit authorization & 96h buffer for EU-residency datasets

Elena —

Thanks for the clear note. Short answers up-front: yes, we can support a 96‑hour transient analytics/telemetry window as a documented, signed exception for your account (Datagrove), but it requires a small set of controls and approvals to be in place before we enable the exception.

What we will do / requirements:
- DPA addendum: sign the addendum that enumerates the 96h exception and describes the conditional failover constraints. We will route the draft for DocuSign to procurement@datagrove.com once we have written confirmation of the requested window.
- Subprocessor roster: we will attach the current roster (operational & analytics subprocessors) and flag any that may be involved in transient hops.
- Ops playbook & evidence: we will provide the transient-egress playbook and a sample audit artifact (log snapshot + KMS key fingerprint) showing a staged replay of a transient hop. Logs are retained for 180 days by default for audit evidence; we can extend retention for a specified legal request window if needed.

Operational guardrails (high level):
- 96h window is enabled as a one-time or recurring exception (you pick cadence). Each enablement requires a programmatic trigger plus a notification email to Datagrove security and a Canary run.
- Notifications: 24-hour pre-notification if scheduled; immediate notification if enabled as an emergency.
- Audit artifacts: per-request telemetry that includes request-id, model variant, egress-region, KMS-key-id, and timestamp; signature using our signing key. We will provide a sample artifact before you sign the addendum.
- Fallback & limits: temporary egress limited to analytics buckets (tagging), you must provide the dataset IDs; no PII-labeled collections allowed in the transient window unless pseudonymized.

Next steps I propose:
1) I attach the DPA addendum draft, subprocessor roster, and the playbook (see attachments).
2) If that looks good, reply with confirmation to enable DocuSign to procurement@datagrove.com and tell us whether you want a recurring 96h cadence or one-off use.
3) Ops (Karthik) will schedule a 30-minute runbook review after signature to walk through evidence and notification flows.

We are targeting Dec 7 for routing to procurement to meet your Dec 10 deadline — can you confirm?

Best,
Mina Haddad
Director, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- DG-DPA-addendum-draft-v1.pdf (DPA addendum draft for Datagrove)
- subprocessor-roster-Dec2027.csv (current roster; analytics subprocessors flagged)
- 96h-transient-egress-playbook.docx (ops runbook, notification & audit flow)
From: Elena Park <elena.park@datagrove.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@datagrove.com
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2027 09:13:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Interim transit authorization & 96h buffer for EU-residency datasets

Mina —

Thanks, that reads well. We reviewed the addendum and the roster with Security. Datagrove is willing to accept the 96h window as an account-level exception with the following small redline requests:
- Add a clause that Datagrove will receive the per-request audit artifact within 4 hours of window activation (we need near-real-time visibility).
- Add a requirement that Redwood escalate to Datagrove security when an unplanned emergency transit occurs (phone + email).

Procurement is ready for DocuSign routing; procurement@datagrove.com will sign once the small redlines are accommodated. Please proceed with the DocuSign envelope and share the link here. Also please upload the example audit artifact into the Drive folder you mentioned for legal review.

Elena
